newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET SHORT, RATES LITTLE CHANGED.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET SHORT, RATES LITTLE CHANGED.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted little changed despite a shortage of cash, dealers said.
They said the Reserve Bank offered Z$100 million worth of treasury bills to discount houses but only Z$50 million were taken up, at 17.56 percent.
Discount houses were selling the 91-day central bank paper in the market at between 17.25 and 17.50 percent while call money ranged from 17.50 to 18 percent.

NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90-days were being bought between 18.25 and 18.50 percent and sold at around 18 percent while bankers acceptance bills were quoted at 18 and 17.25 percent (buying and selling respectively).
Reserve Bank figures showed the market closed Z$182.2 million short on Wednesday from a Z$112 million deficit on Tuesday.
